item.title: Breath and Fullness: John 1:1-18, James 1:1-11, Ecclesiastes 1
item.description:
John 1:1-18, James 1:1-11, Ecclesiastes 1
Three books begin at once. John opens with the eternal Word who became flesh and tabernacled among us, James tells us to count trials joy and ask God for wisdom, and the Preacher in Ecclesiastes calls everything under the sun a breath. A morning about what we cannot produce and what is freely given. item.title: Hands Raised: Proverbs 31, Luke 24, Hebrews 13
item.description:
Luke 24:45-53, Hebrews 13:9-25, Proverbs 31
The risen Jesus opens the minds of his friends and blesses them as he ascends, hebrews calls us outside the camp to follow him, and Proverbs ends with a portrait of a woman who fears the Lord. item.title: Touch Me and See: Proverbs 30, Luke 24, Hebrews 13
item.description:

item.title: We Had Hoped: Proverbs 29, Luke 24, Hebrews 12
item.description:
Luke 24:13-27, Hebrews 12:1-13, Proverbs 29:1-14
On the Emmaus road two disciples walk away from Jerusalem saying 'we had hoped', and Jesus opens the Scriptures to them. Hebrews 12 calls the struggle a father's training, and Proverbs 29 asks whether you will bend your neck or stiffen it. item.title: The Borrowed Tomb: Proverbs 28, Luke 23, Hebrews 11
item.description:
Luke 23:50-56, Hebrews 11:17-31, Proverbs 28:1-14
Joseph of Arimathea, a council member who kept his faith quiet, walks into Pilate's headquarters and asks for a body. Today we read his burial of Jesus in Luke, Abraham's reasoning on the mountain and Moses' choices in Hebrews 11, and a Proverbs 28 chapter about boldness and confession. item.title: Forgive Them: Proverbs 26, Luke 23, Hebrews 10
item.description:
Luke 23:32-37, Hebrews 10:1-18, Proverbs 26:17-28
Proverbs warns about meddlers, whisperers and smooth talkers, Luke 23 reaches the cross where Jesus prays 'Father, forgive them', and Hebrews 10 explains why one sacrifice finished what thousands could not. item.title: Green Wood and Dry: Proverbs 26, Luke 23, Hebrews 9
item.description:
Proverbs 26:1-16, Luke 23:26-31, Hebrews 9:11-28
The first episode of Morning Mercies joins the Navigators plan at month nine, day sixteen. We read Proverbs 26 on answering fools and the sluggard's imaginary lion, walk the road to the cross with Simon of Cyrene and the weeping women of Jerusalem in Luke 23, and follow Christ into heaven itself with his own blood in Hebrews 9. With Calvin, Chrysostom, Gregory the Great, Matthew Henry, Matthew Poole, John Gill, Spurgeon, R.C. Sproul and John Piper.
